_about: The hand-owned half of il/data/app/district-search.json, which lets the search box answer '33rd ward' or 'State Senate District 7'. Each entry names a layer and the OFFICIAL NAME of one of its districts with the number taken out ('Ward' for 'Ward 33'). The app derives the variants a reader types from that name — 'Ward 33', 'ward #33', 'ward no. 33', '33rd ward', '33 ward' — and also accepts the layer's own sidebar label ('City Ward 33'), which the builder copies from metro-worksheet.json so the two cannot disagree. An entry whose districts belong to one city carries `where`: the result names it ('City Ward · Chicago') so a reader in a suburb with its own Ward 3 is not handed Chicago's without being told, and a query may include it ('Chicago Ward 33'). The DISTRICTS are never listed here: scripts/build_district_search.py reads them from each layer's own source, and its --check fails if this file names a layer the app does not register. A layer belongs here when 'District 3' names one district: either its numbering is unique across its whole ground, or it is county-dispatched and each district carries its county, which the query must then name ('Lake County Board District 3'). A layer whose districts are NAMED rather than numbered — the statewide school districts and CPS's attendance zones — carries `"match": "name"`: each district is found by its own name ('Galesburg school district', 'Curie high school'), with or without its number, and `name` here is only the kind of district, used for the hint shown before a name is typed. Suburban wards and precincts, whose numbers repeat per town, are left out until they have a way to say which.

layers.name: Ward
layers.why: Chicago's 50 wards. The layer also holds suburban wards, whose numbers repeat town to town, so only the City's own dataset is indexed.

layers.name: Police District
layers.why: CPD's 22 districts, numbered once city-wide. '9th Police District' is derived; CPD's own bare '9th District' is not, because 'district 9' names a district in every layer here and would be a guess about which one.

layers.name: School Board District
layers.why: The Chicago Board of Education's 20 seats, each named as the Board and the ballot name it, by a number and a letter (District 1a .. District 10b): 'school board district 2b', 'school board 2b', '2 b'. The boundary file also numbers them 1-20, which is its row order and nothing a reader sees, so internal_numbers keeps that number out of every name and every match. A bare number names the Board's own district, which is two seats: 'school board district 4' finds 4a and 4b. The sub-district aliases are accepted as typed input only, since readers may know the seats by that word; nothing shows it.

layers.name: Congressional District
layers.why: The census file's own name for each of Illinois's 17 districts.

layers.name: State Senate District
layers.why: The census file's own name for each of Illinois's 59 districts.

layers.name: State House District
layers.why: The census file's own name for each of Illinois's 118 districts.

layers.name: Supreme Court District
layers.why: The Illinois Supreme Court's 5 judicial districts.

layers.name: Board of Review District
layers.why: The Cook County Board of Review's 3 districts.

layers.name: Unified School District
layers.why: Census TIGER's 387 Illinois unified (K-12) districts, Chicago Public Schools among them as District 299. Numbers repeat across the state (36 are District 1), so a district is found by its name: 'Galesburg school district', 'Galesburg 205', 'Galesburg CUSD 205'. A number alone finds only the few districts whose name has no place in it ('Community Unit School District 300').

layers.name: High School District
layers.why: Census TIGER's 105 Illinois high school districts, where elementary and high school districts are separate. Several carry no place name ('Township High School District 214'), so 'District 214' finds those.

layers.name: Elementary School District
layers.why: Census TIGER's 371 Illinois elementary districts: 'Evanston 65', 'Evanston CCSD 65'.

layers.name: Elementary School Zone
layers.why: CPS's elementary attendance zones, one per school, named as the card names them: 'Metcalfe elementary', 'Alcott ES'.

layers.name: Middle School Zone
layers.why: CPS's middle-school attendance zones, where middle schools are zoned separately.

layers.name: High School Zone
layers.why: CPS's high school attendance zones: 'Curie high school', 'Curie HS'.

layers.name: County Board District
layers.why: Every county the county-board layer dispatches, read through the app's own per-county loaders. Every county has a District 3, so each result carries its county and a query must name it ('Lake County Board District 3', 'Lake Board District 3'). 'County Commissioner District' is how Cook names its districts ('Cook County Commissioner District 3'), and 'Commissioner District' how the commission-form counties do. Numbered and lettered districts are indexed; Menard's named ones are not (see SKIP in the builder).
